newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP selected Bayu-Undan gas operator.
newsitem.headline: BHP selected Bayu-Undan gas operator.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd's Petroleum division said on Wednesday it had been selected as the unit operator of the joint Bayu-Undan gas condensate field in the Timor Sea between northern Australia and Indonesia.
"The selection was confirmed by the participants of both the 91-12 and 91-13 joint ventures in Melbourne late last week," BHP Petroleum said.
BHP holds 42.42 percent of the ZOCA (Zone of Cooperation Agreement) 91-12 "Undan" permit, while Phillips Petroleum Co leads the ZOCA 91-13 "Bayu" consortium.
The Bayu-Undan field was last estimated to have proved plus probable reserves of 3.1 trillion cubic feet and development of the field has been estimated to cost up to A$4 billion.
BHP said both joint ventures had collectively studied various development concepts for the field over the last nine months, covering both liquids and gas production.
"A decision on a possible liquefied natural gas (LNG) project, whether based offshore or onshore, is expected to be made in the near future," said BHP.
Petroz NL, which has 13.371 percent of ZOCA 91-12, said the form of upstream development had been decided on.

"The upstream phase of the project consists of a liquids stripping/gas recycling operation whereby condensate and LPG are separated from the gas stream offshore and transported by tankers to market," Petroz said in a separate statement.
"It is expected that the offshore liquids recovery project will be integrated with an LNG production facility," Petroz said.
"Both offshore and onshore locations for the LNG facilities are under consideration," it said.
"Field development is expected to commence in 1998 leading to first production of condensate and LPG in 2001."
Northern Territory ministers are confident that BHP and Phillips will choose an onshore LNG plant with a 470 km pipeline to bring the gas from the Timor Sea.
Reports have put the cost of such a plant at between A$1 billion to A$1.9 billion.
Phillips is seen favouring an onshore plant while BHP has favoured an offshore plant.
Santos Ltd has a 21.426 percent stake in ZOCA 91-12, while Indonesia's Inpex Sahul has 21.21 percent.
The adjacent ZOCA 91-13 permit is operated by Phillips, which holds 60 percent. Oryx Energy Co of the U.S. has 25 percent and Britain's Hardy Oil & Gas Plc 15 percent.
"The single field extends across both contract areas and any developoment will be carried out under the framework of a unitisation agreement and utilise shared facilities," BHP said.
Petroz said the start of production at the nearby Elang/Kakatua oil fields in mid-1998 would make a major contribution to its funding obligations for the Bayu-Undan development.
An onshore plant would produce an estimated three million tonnes of LNG a year.
